claims.text: The lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) generates \(J_v\); the cited theorem proves its minimality. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
For every valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), no nonzero homogeneous syzygy of the lower-adjoined form exists. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 270-304]

Let \(q=n-r\), \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\), and \[ v^\vee=v_{q,\;q+j-i,\;q-i+1,\;n}. \] Then \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian, its parameters are \[ (i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b), \] and \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong \bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})} \mathbb Z[\bar s_\mu]. \] Hence \(G_R\) is an integral homogeneous basis of indecomposables, is an irredundant generating family of \(J_v\), and \[ \operatorname{Hilb}_{J_v/A_+J_v}(z) =z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z. \]
